newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia considers defence export barter deals.
newsitem.headline: Australia considers defence export barter deals.

text.p: Australia may accept commodities instead of cash as a way of promoting its defence exports, Defence Industry Minister Bronwyn Bishop said on Saturday.
The Australia defence industry was too reliant on the Australi, Bishop told Reuters.
"To get the exports I want to look at...countertrade -- counter-purchasing if you like, where payment is in the commodity, or partial payment is in the commodity," she said.
Australia was not familiar with such methods, she said, but there were trading houses specialised in it.
Australian industry supplies much of the equipment for its own forces, especially the navy, which has not bought a major new ship from a foreign shipyard for more than 10 years.
But little equipment is exported, although the privately held contractor Transfield is seeking to sell more than 20 patrol ships to Malaysia.
